payload.title: File:Xenodontolacerta fangi (holotype, dentition).png
payload.artist_html: J. Jiang, L.-P. Dong, X. Xu, A. Bi, & S. Evans
payload.credit_html: "A new polyglyphanodontian lizard from the Upper Cretaceous of southern China implies a complex evolutionary history of the clade"
payload.description_html: The dentition of Xenodontolacerta fangi (holotype CVEB20180206). (a) Anterior view of the premaxilla: the red dashed line along the midline indicates the absence of a median tooth in the premaxilla, and four red small arrows point at the three preserved premaxillary teeth and one vacant tooth position on the left side; (b) right lateral view of the upper and lower dentition; (c) left lateral view of the fragmentary upper and lower dentition: yellow squares indicate the location of the teeth in (d,e); (d) three-dimensional rendering of three posteromedial dentary teeth in labial (i), occlusal (ii) and lingual (iii) views; (e) three-dimensional rendering of three posterior dentary teeth in labial (i), occlusal (ii) and lingual (iii) views. In (d,e), a and p (short for anterior and posterior, respectively) with arrows indicate the orientation of the teeth. * indicates the small triangular surface anterior to the lingual depression.
